questions.prompt: Before connecting Okta to a new application, which fact set is most useful to establish?

options.text: Environment, provider roles, endpoints, identifiers, account rules, required claims and access requirements
options.explanation: These define the actual trust and account contract rather than merely the transport settings.

options.text: Only the application's logo dimensions
options.explanation: Branding does not define federation behavior.

options.text: Only the number of employees
options.explanation: User count alone does not establish the integration contract.

options.text: Only whether a sample XML file opens
options.explanation: Readability is not a requirements agreement.

questions.prompt: Staging and production use different entity IDs and ACS URLs. What should a handover preserve?

options.text: An explicit mapping of each environment to its own settings and owners
options.explanation: Clear environment mapping prevents valid-looking settings from being applied to the wrong trust relationship.

options.text: One unlabeled screenshot containing mixed settings
options.explanation: Ambiguous evidence invites environment confusion.

options.text: A rule to accept both audiences everywhere
options.explanation: That weakens environment separation rather than documenting it.

options.text: Only the most recently used URL
options.explanation: Recency does not identify the correct environment.

questions.prompt: An app team proposes matching users by display name because it is easy to read. What should be resolved?

options.text: A unique, stable, scoped identifier and a defined account-matching rule
options.explanation: Readable names can be duplicated or changed; identity resolution needs a stronger agreement.

options.text: Only require a nonempty display name
options.explanation: A nonempty value can still be duplicated, mutable or incorrectly scoped.

options.text: A rule to select the most privileged duplicate
options.explanation: Privilege is not evidence of identity.

options.text: A promise that signatures prevent duplicate names
options.explanation: Cryptographic protection does not make name values unique.

questions.prompt: A new integration disables JIT provisioning. What should the rollout plan include?

options.text: How eligible accounts will be created, assigned, changed and disabled through the agreed lifecycle process
options.explanation: A SAML response cannot resolve an absent account when automatic creation is not enabled.

options.text: An assumption that first sign-in creates every account anyway
options.explanation: That contradicts the stated configuration.

options.text: Only a longer assertion lifetime
options.explanation: Timing does not create accounts.

options.text: An assumption that app assignment is the same as downstream account creation
options.explanation: Assignment and provisioning are separate unless the actual integration explicitly connects them.

questions.prompt: An application needs employee ID and department for its agreed functions. A proposed assertion also includes home address and personal phone. What should the team do?

options.text: Release only justified attributes required by the integration
options.explanation: Unnecessary personal data increases exposure without helping the defined access function.

options.text: Send all available profile fields for convenience
options.explanation: Availability is not a reason to disclose every field.

options.text: Encrypt the assertion and stop reviewing attribute need
options.explanation: Encryption does not make unnecessary disclosure necessary.

options.text: Move the extra data into RelayState
options.explanation: That relocates exposure instead of removing it.

questions.prompt: The IdP team controls authentication policy, and the app team controls local resource roles. What should planning capture?

options.text: Which team owns each requirement, configuration decision and failure boundary
options.explanation: Clear ownership prevents authentication success from being confused with application authorization readiness.

options.text: A rule that either team can silently override all settings
options.explanation: That removes controlled ownership and evidence.

options.text: Only the signing-certificate owner, because claims and roles are automatic
options.explanation: Claims issuance and local authorization require their own ownership and configuration.

options.text: No app-team participation because SAML is involved
options.explanation: The SP still owns crucial account and authorization decisions.

questions.prompt: A sign-in works while the tester already has an active app session. What additional test is needed?

options.text: A controlled new sign-in with relevant app and IdP session states recorded
options.explanation: The existing app session may have bypassed the federation path being tested.

options.text: Only refresh the same authenticated page
options.explanation: That can continue to test session reuse rather than federation.

options.text: Only change the page theme
options.explanation: Theme changes do not create a controlled authentication baseline.

options.text: Conclude all SAML paths have passed
options.explanation: One existing-session path is insufficient evidence.

questions.prompt: Why include wrong-audience, expired, replayed and incorrectly correlated responses in a test plan?

options.text: To verify that the receiver rejects cases outside the trust and acceptance contract
options.explanation: Success-path testing alone does not show enforcement of the intended boundaries.

options.text: To make production accept more kinds of malformed messages
options.explanation: The purpose is to confirm rejection, not broaden acceptance.

options.text: To replace all positive sign-in tests
options.explanation: Positive and rejection tests establish different facts.

options.text: To prove every authentication policy was evaluated correctly
options.explanation: These rejection tests exercise receiver boundaries; policy assurance requires its own relevant evidence.

questions.prompt: Okta's attribute preview shows employeeNumber, but the live SP sign-in still fails. What evidence is needed next?

options.text: The actual issued response and receiver result for the same controlled sign-in
options.explanation: Preview is useful configuration evidence, but runtime issuance and consumption must be confirmed.

options.text: Only another screenshot of the same preview
options.explanation: Repeating preview does not establish live delivery or mapping.

options.text: Only the IdP metadata file
options.explanation: Metadata helps describe trust and endpoints, but does not prove the actual released claims and local matching outcome.

options.text: A declaration that preview guarantees acceptance
options.explanation: The receiver can still reject the message or account mapping.

questions.prompt: A change ticket says K2 is configured centrally. What evidence best establishes rollover readiness?

options.text: K2 is trusted by every active validating runtime, and controlled K2 sign-ins pass
options.explanation: Saved configuration and actual runtime adoption are distinct.

options.text: The certificate file has a new name
options.explanation: A name does not establish adoption.

options.text: One browser has loaded the settings page
options.explanation: Browser viewing is not server-side verification readiness.

options.text: One successful K2 login on one of several nodes
options.explanation: One node's result does not establish readiness across all active validators.

questions.prompt: A planned change has no tested recovery path and could block all administrators from the app. What should happen before release?

options.text: Establish and verify an authorized recovery route with clear ownership and criteria
options.explanation: Recovery needs to be concrete before an access-affecting change is activated.

options.text: Disable all validation preemptively
options.explanation: Removing trust checks is not a sound recovery plan.

options.text: Rely on the same federated admin route being changed
options.explanation: That route may be unavailable during the failure the recovery plan needs to address.

options.text: Give every user the provider's private key
options.explanation: Private-key distribution would create a serious trust failure.

questions.prompt: A rollout's old signing key is uncompromised, but the new key fails on one node. Which response is best planned in advance?

options.text: A bounded recovery or rollback procedure tied to observed failure and the key-trust state
options.explanation: A useful rollback plan names what changes, who acts and what proves recovery.

options.text: Always keep both keys trusted forever
options.explanation: Indefinite overlap avoids a retirement decision rather than defining recovery.

options.text: Always delete every trusted key immediately
options.explanation: That may turn a partial failure into complete outage.

options.text: Change all users' department attributes
options.explanation: That is unrelated to the failing verification node.

questions.prompt: A test user can sign in but sees an unexpected finance role. Is the integration ready just because authentication passed?

options.text: No; identity mapping and authorization outcomes must also match the requirements
options.explanation: A wrong account or wrong role can be a more serious failure than a visible sign-in error.

options.text: Yes; any application role is acceptable after SSO
options.explanation: Authentication does not justify unintended permissions.

options.text: Yes; a signed groups attribute cannot be mis-mapped
options.explanation: Protected values can still be mapped incorrectly by the application.

options.text: Only confirm that the account's display name looks familiar
options.explanation: A familiar label does not prove the correct unique identity and permission set.

questions.prompt: A business requirement says "logout everywhere." What must be clarified before implementation?

options.text: Which sessions, apps and devices are in scope, what mechanisms support them and how completion is confirmed
options.explanation: A broad phrase must be translated into supported and testable session outcomes.

options.text: Only the text of the logout button
options.explanation: Button text cannot establish cross-system session termination.

options.text: An assumption that local logout covers all providers
options.explanation: Local and federated session scopes differ.

options.text: Assume account deactivation will satisfy every logout requirement
options.explanation: Lifecycle changes and immediate session termination have different scope and support requirements.

questions.prompt: An integration has a failing NameID match and a proposed certificate rollover. What improves diagnosis?

options.text: Separate the changes where practical and record a controlled baseline for each boundary
options.explanation: Changing unrelated trust and identity settings at once obscures causes and recovery evidence.

options.text: Change every setting until one attempt succeeds
options.explanation: Uncontrolled changes produce weak causal evidence.

options.text: Disable signature validation to simplify all tests
options.explanation: That invalidates important security checks.

options.text: Test only with a pre-existing local session
options.explanation: That may skip both changed federation behaviors.

questions.prompt: What should a release's monitoring plan compare?

options.text: Issuer-side events, receiver outcomes and user-visible results for the same controlled attempts
options.explanation: Cross-boundary evidence helps distinguish issuance, acceptance, account and access failures.

options.text: Only whether the public home page loads
options.explanation: Availability of a public page does not prove federation success.

options.text: Only the count of successful IdP events
options.explanation: Issuer-side counts do not by themselves confirm receiver acceptance and the intended local account outcome.

options.text: Only one unrelated historical log entry
options.explanation: Uncorrelated evidence cannot establish the current result.

questions.prompt: Which handover entry is most useful to the next engineer?

options.text: The exact environment, expected values, owners, test evidence, known limitations and recovery procedure
options.explanation: A handover should support investigation and safe change without reconstructing the project from memory.

options.text: "SSO works" with no date or test context
options.explanation: That statement does not establish what was tested or where.

options.text: A collection of private keys
options.explanation: Secrets do not belong in routine handover documentation.

options.text: An unlabeled assertion copied from an unknown tenant
options.explanation: Unknown provenance makes evidence difficult to use safely.

questions.prompt: A required replay-rejection test has not run, but one positive sign-in passed. What should the release status say?

options.text: The defined acceptance evidence is incomplete
options.explanation: A missing required test cannot be converted into a pass by success elsewhere.

options.text: All requirements are proved because one user signed in
options.explanation: A positive baseline does not establish that a replayed response is rejected for the intended reason.

options.text: Replay protection is unnecessary for signed messages
options.explanation: Signed assertions can be replayed unless reuse is detected.

options.text: The failed evidence should be removed from the plan
options.explanation: Removing a requirement after the fact hides the gap.

questions.prompt: An organization plans to change the value used as NameID from email to employee ID. What needs assessment?

options.text: Both issuance and the SP's mapping, account-linking, uniqueness and migration behavior
options.explanation: Changing the identifier can change which account is resolved, not merely the appearance of XML.

options.text: Only whether employee IDs contain digits
options.explanation: Syntax alone does not cover identity continuity.

options.text: Only the signing algorithm
options.explanation: Signing preserves the new value but does not migrate local account associations.

options.text: Nothing if both values identify the same human informally
options.explanation: The receiver uses configured matching rules rather than human intuition.

questions.prompt: A handover states, "We plan to enable front-channel logout next month." How should this be interpreted?

options.text: As a future proposal, not proof that the current integration terminates participating app sessions
options.explanation: Documented intent and verified current behavior are different states.

options.text: As a completed end-to-end logout test
options.explanation: A plan is not execution evidence.

options.text: As proof every browser supports the feature
options.explanation: That needs separate verification.

options.text: As a reason to delete current session test results
options.explanation: Current evidence remains necessary.
